hed: Trump: U.S. could stay in Iran and ‘keep the oil’; asks Zelenskyy to spare Russian diesel
dek: At the Irish Open in Doonbeg on Sunday, President Trump said the United States could “stay and keep the oil” in Iran, comparing that option to his administration’s Venezuela oil arrangement, and added that Venezuela revenue had “paid for the war many times.” He said the Iran war may end around or just after the November midterms and that gasoline would then “drop like a rock.” NBC News reported he also told reporters he had asked Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to stop targeting Russian diesel/refining infrastructure because those strikes were “hurting the world” amid record U.S. diesel prices. Monday crude still jumped toward $108.

byline: Event summary from public reporting and named outlets

cl.body: Reuters, The Hill, and NBC News lead with Trump’s Doonbeg “keep the oil” Iran option beside the Venezuela parallel, his midterms-timed war-end forecast, and his reported ask that Zelenskyy stop hitting Russian diesel — as Monday’s $108 Brent print and AAA’s $6.23 diesel record underscored the energy stakes he was describing.

cr.body: Arab News, Al Arabiya English, and CNA stress Trump’s Sunday forecast that the Iran war ends around or after the midterms with gasoline set to “drop like a rock,” his insistence on the “right deal,” and the Venezuela revenue claim — while NBC’s diesel-ask reporting ties his Doonbeg remarks to Monday’s record U.S. diesel average.
